adapter_description: Cook's membrane: 2D tapered panel with vertices (0,0), (48,44), (48,60), (0,44), plane strain, compressible neo-Hookean (same psi as B1), E = 1000, nu = 0.3 (constant), total Lagrangian. Left edge x = 0 clamped; right edge x = 48 loaded by a uniform dead shear traction t_y = 5 (total 80) in 10 equal increments; top and bottom edges traction-free. Q4 elements, 2x2 Gauss, on an N x N mapped mesh of the parametric square, N = 4, 8, ..., 256 (h = 1/N, ratio 2). Strategies at N = 64: uniform and grading toward the clamped edge and both left corners (a = 0.5, 0.8; corner elements 2x and 5x smaller, same element count). QoIs: u_tip, v_tip = displacement of the corner (48,60), a mesh node on every level; max_disp_mag over the nodes; strain_energy = stored energy; interior_avg_PK1_frob = detJ-weighted mean of |P|_F over the Gauss points inside the disc of radius 4 centred at (24,40); interior_gk_PK1_frob = the same with the smooth weight exp(-(d/3)^2); peak_PK1_frob = max |P|_F over all Gauss points. Corner theory (singularity.py, Williams eigenproblem, clamped/free, plane strain, nu = 0.3): the 47.5-degree corner at (0,0) is regular; the 108.4-degree corner at (0,44) has lam = 0.6442, so energy converges at order 2 lam = 1.29, point values at >= 1.29 and the peak grows like h^(lam-1) = h^-0.356. Solver: scikit-fem with the residual/tangent of independent_solver.py. No surrogate errors are recorded, so the class ceilings apply.
